sources.entry: Karabiner-Elements - Karabiner-Elements is a powerful utility for keyboard customization on macOS Sierra (10.12) or later.

summary.one_liner: Karabiner-Elements is a key remapper for macOS that customizes keyboard behavior, distributed as a package and buildable from source.
summary.what_it_does: The README describes Karabiner-Elements as a key remapper for macOS. It can be downloaded from the official site or installed with Homebrew via `brew install --cask karabiner-elements`. Supported systems are listed as macOS 13 Ventura through macOS 27 Golden Gate, with Apple Silicon noted as the only option for the newest release. The README links to external documentation for usage and to a localization guide for translations. A developer section explains how to build a signed package with `make package` on Xcode, including code signing identity setup and how to reset macOS permissions when switching from the official build to a self-built one. It also notes pre-built binaries and Swift packages (such as Sparkle) used during the build.
use_cases: remap keyboard keys on a Mac
install a key remapper with Homebrew
sign and package a custom keyboard remapper build
notable: Runs background services that require code signing, and macOS permissions are tied to the signing identity
Can be installed via Homebrew cask
Build instructions cover both Apple Developer Program and non-enrolled code signing setups
Includes a DriverKit virtual HID device package as a pre-built binary
caveats: Building from source requires macOS 15+, Xcode 26+, and several Homebrew tools
Permissions must be re-granted when switching between official and self-built packages
Usage documentation is linked externally rather than included in the README
